subject: MAP: cost decomposition + caching/batching validation for PulseHealth pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: cost decomposition + caching/batching validation for PulseHealth pilot

Hi Sarah —

Following our MAP sync today, I wanted to capture the outstanding cost items we need validated before we lock the pilot economics and close timeline. I've attached a single-sheet workbook with the assumptions currently baked into the MAP (MAP_Cost_Assumptions_v3.xlsx). Key asks:

- Tokenization baseline: confirm expected average tokens per interaction for the LLM prompts/responses you plan to send (we've modelled 350 tokens/interaction).
- Caching scope: are 30% of requests eligible for prefix/KV reuse (session-based or identical prompts)? We model 30% cache hit for the first pass.
- Batching tolerance: your frontend can accept up to ~120ms added latency for batching to yield the modeled 20% unit-cost reduction; confirm acceptable latency budget.
- Peak shape & burst: confirm 95th percentile concurrent requests and if there are predictable hourly peaks (we need this to size reserved capacity for Dedicated during the pilot).

If you can reply with a short line-item confirmation for tokens, cache-hit %, batching latency tolerance, and 95p concurrent RPS, we can finalize the MAP numbers and publish the mutual milestones for procurement.

Attachment: MAP_Cost_Assumptions_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet -- single sheet: assumptions & calc)

Next steps after your confirmations: we run a quick ops simulation (we'll share results), finalize the financials in the MAP, and hand the SOW to contracts. Target to sign pilot SOW within 10 business days after confirmations.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <contracts@pulsehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: cost decomposition + caching/batching validation for PulseHealth pilot

Marissa —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick confirmations below (we'll follow up with a short note from Product Ops tomorrow with a sample trace):

- Tokens per interaction: our current prototype averages ~420 tokens per user request + ~160 tokens for the assistant reply = ~580 total tokens; however, typical clinical summary flows should trim to ~420 average once we trim metadata. For the pilot, use 500 tokens/interaction as a conservative mid-point.
- Caching: ~20% of requests are identical (templated prompts) and an additional ~10% are session-prefix re-useable. So 30% cache-eligible overall (matches your model).
- Batching latency tolerance: engineering prefers not to exceed 75ms added tail latency for end-user flows; for background ingestion we can accept more aggressive batching.
- 95p concurrent requests: on pilot traffic profile expect 18 concurrency at 95p during daytime peak; bursts up to ~35 for short windows (we can flag those bursts in the MAP).

We attached the product trace to a follow-up deck internally; procurement (contracts@pulsehealth.com) is looped for SOW timing.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Product, PulseHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MAP: cost decomposition + caching/batching validation for PulseHealth pilot

Marissa / Kim —

Thanks, Sarah — that clarifies a lot. I ran a quick ops-sim with the updated 500 tokens/interaction and the 30% effective cache hit. Attached are the CSV outputs from the sim (ops-sim-results.csv). Highlights:

- Units/tokens: at 500 tokens/interaction, tokens per second during the daytime 95p window (18 concurrency assumed, 0.8 req/s per concurrent session) maps to ~7,200 tokens/s.
- Batching uplift: if we allow 75ms added latency we saw ~18% reduction in tokens-per-dollar in our simulation (microbatching and token-level prefetching enabled).
- Burst handling: short bursts to 35 concurrency increase peak GPU memory pressure; with our fallback routing to a quantized variant we can preserve latency SLOs but will increase per-token cost by ~22% for those windows.

Operational asks before we finalize MAP numbers:
- Can Procurement sign off on a three-week pilot SOW with a capped pilot spend (we've modeled a $25k cap to limit exposure)?
- Kim: please confirm whether the team wants us to bake in a conservative 15% premium for burst windows in the MAP or model bursts as a separate add-on line item.

Attachment: ops-sim-results.csv (simulation outputs -- rows: minute, concurrency, tokens/s, cost_per_minute)

-Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>, PulseHealth Procurement <contracts@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MAP: cost decomposition + caching/batching validation for PulseHealth pilot

Sarah / Contracts team —

Appreciate the fast turn. Updated plan & asks below so we have a single source-of-truth in the MAP before SOW:

1) Economics we will publish in MAP (conservative):
   - Tokens per interaction: 500 (per confirmed prod estimate).
   - Cache hit: 30% effective (templated + session prefixes).
   - Batching latency: cap 75ms added; modeling assumes 18% unit-cost reduction when batching is permitted at that latency.
   - Pilot spend cap: $25,000 (we'll include an overage clause and auto-notify at 80% cap).

2) Burst treatment:
   - We will model bursts as an add-on; we will assume a 15% premium to the baseline unit price for quantized fallback windows. Ben, thanks for the sim — Kim to confirm final call on the premium but please proceed with 15% as the MAP placeholder.

3) Timeline:
   - Today: we update the MAP and push the spreadsheet to the shared Drive.
   - 11/05 EOD: Redwood to share final MAP sheet and the updated mutual milestones.
   - 11/12: Target SOW signature date (subject to procurement review).

Links: Drive folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_MapCost_PulseHealth (MAP_Cost_Assumptions_v3.xlsx + ops-sim-results.csv)
HubSpot deal: HubSpot://deals/HLX-3721

If that plan looks good, Contracts can return a redline timeline and we will start SOW drafting on our side today.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
